messages:
Maria Chen: FYI — prod firewall policy deployed last night (fw-2026-03-19-3). After that a subset of us-west-2 GPU nodes failed to join the warm pool. Seeing 503s on /v1/infer and slow cold starts. Anyone digging?
Raj Patel: I started a pass. provisioning-agent logs show repeated KMS Decrypt failures during node bootstrap: "AccessDenied" for role arn:aws:iam::...:instance-role/gpu-node.
Jen Ortega: Confirmed. VPC flow logs show blocked egress to keystore endpoint 10.12.8.5 from subnets tagged `gpu-prod`. The new deny rule targets subnets without the `egress-allowed` tag — looks like those instances lost the tag during a terraform refactor.
Leo Park: Oof. Which rule specifically? Is this an SG or NACL rule? I can rollback the firewall policy if needed.
Maria Chen: It's a managed policy pushed by the fw team (id fw-2026-03-19-3). I think it created a deny on destination 10.12.0.0/16 for subnets matching tag `env:prod` without `egress-allowed`.
ops-bot: deploymentbot: rollout fw-2026-03-19-3 -> completed on us-west-2 at 2026-03-19T23:42:10Z (by emmily).
Raj Patel: Quick mitigation: provisioning will work if KMS decrypt works -> which needs egress to keystore. We can either: 1) rollback fw policy, or 2) add an explicit allow for keystore + kms endpoints for gpu-prod subnets.
Jen Ortega: Adding allow is safer. Can we scope to instance role/ENIs? The deny was broad and intended to lock dev subnets. But tags got inconsistent.
Leo Park: Patching policy now to insert allow rule for 10.12.8.5/32 and kms endpoints (kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com). Applying in staging first.
Maria Chen: Note: while this is fixed, warm pool depletion caused autoscaler to spin up on-demand nodes -> huge NAT GW egress and data transfer costs spiked. We already have a cost alert for NAT bytes.
Raj Patel: We saw NAT gateway bytes jump 6x for 30m. Billing team alerted. If we keep falling back to on-demand, monthly run rate could increase materially.
Jen Ortega: Mitigation checklist: 
- Add allow rule for keystore + KMS (scoped to gpu-prod subnets)
- Re-tag mis-tagged subnets/instances (terraform state fix)
- Backfill runbook to test keystore reachability during firewall rollout
- Add an automated smoke that probes KMS decrypt during policy canary

Can someone own each?
Leo Park: I’ll push the allow and run the staging test. then apply to prod canary (10% of subnets).
Maria Chen: I’ll take tagging and terraform fix. Raj, can you handle the smoke test + runbook updates?
Raj Patel: Yep. I’ll add an e2e step that attempts a node bootstrap with a KMS decrypt. Also adding an alert when warm pool capacity < 50% and provisioning errors > 5/min.
ops-bot: monitorbot: alert created: warm-pool-capacity-low (threshold 50%) — created by raj.p — alert id ALRT-7621.
Jen Ortega: After allow applied in staging, I validated KMS decrypts succeed and instances rejoined warm pool. Pushing to prod canary now.
Leo Park: Prod canary applied to 12 subnets. Observing logs — successful KMS decrypts, warm pool nodes healthy. Rolling the rest in 10m.
Maria Chen: Rolling back is unnecessary now, but we should treat this as a near-miss. Two follow-ups: 1) change firewall rollout playbook to include keystore/KMS reachability smoke, 2) avoid tag-only gating for critical infra paths (tags can drift).
Raj Patel: Also adding a guard in provisioning-agent: fallback to local cached keys for a short window if KMS unreachable (with audit log) so we don't instantly OOM warm pool.
Jen Ortega: FYI finance: need a postmortem on the NAT cost spike. Rough estimate: 30m * peak NAT throughput => ~ $12k. tagging for chargeback.
Maria Chen: Thanks. Closing timeline: root cause = new deny rule + tag drift -> blocked KMS egress -> node boot failures -> warm pool drop -> on-demand spin-up -> NAT cost spike.
Leo Park: I'll attach the policy diff and the staging->prod rollout notes to the ticket.
Maria Chen: Good job team. Filing follow-up ticket for: firewall canary tests, terraform tag validation, provisioning-agent fallback, cost retro.
ops-bot: ticketbot: created TKT-4897 "firewall rollout: keystore smoke + tag validation" assigned to eng-infra.
Raj Patel: leaving a quick snippet for the smoke test: 
```bash
# attempt KMS decrypt from a canary runner
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --region us-west-2 --profile canary-runner
# expect HTTP 200 and plaintext out
```
Maria Chen: closing thread once ticket has PRs. :white_check_mark:
